better_but_spec_change.why_not_taken: KITS defines the RL action indices (9 = kit[0], 10 = kit[1]); a one-ability tagger kit takes the action space from 11 to 10 and invalidates every 11-action checkpoint. The dial-only form is within 0.013 of it.

dead_dials.DESTINY_ARM_TIME: near-inert: ChasePolicy spends the gate on the tick after arming, so the window length has never been the binding constraint.
dead_dials.DESTINY_MIN/MAX/PREFERRED_DIST: NO LONGER DEAD (pass 2), but now nearly inert: 3/4/5 -> 8/10/13 moves the seven-map mean by +1.1 pp, inside the n=24 standard error. The +12 pp reported in pass 1 was the tagger gating itself away from the runner.
dead_dials.JOURNEY_DEPTH: still inert on the shipped maps: 3 -> 5 changes the seven-map result by 0 (no map has a 4-5 tile block between two open regions), and 3 -> 2 would REMOVE candidates, because journey_preview treats the depth as a cap.
dead_dials.STASIS_RANGE: NO LONGER DEAD (pass 2). 120/160/200/280 px now give 0.250/0.387/0.429/0.423 on the seven-map suite. Direction is counter-intuitive: a shorter range is a TAGGER buff, because the policy fires as soon as the target is in range, so the range is really a cast-timing dial.

engine_and_policy_fixes.chase_policy: reads world.skill_tuning.STASIS_RANGE (minus a 0.5-tile slack) and world.skill_tuning.DESTINY_MAX_DIST instead of a hard-coded 4.5 tiles and a module-scope import.
engine_and_policy_fixes.engine: World.step only spends the tick's movement on a cast that LANDS; a refused cast falls through to the caller's (dx, dy). Cast attempts/refusals counted per role and per ability.
engine_and_policy_fixes.engine_journey_spec: unchanged. JOURNEY_DEPTH 2 would REDUCE castability (the depth is a cap, not a floor), and the policy fix alone made the one-out ablation non-negative, so the early-collapse and runner-only variants were not taken.
engine_and_policy_fixes.flee_policy: journey is priced, not panic-triggered: cast when the carve cuts the BFS route to the current objective by JOURNEY_GAIN=4 tiles AND the tagger's last-seen position is >= JOURNEY_SAFE_MARGIN=2 tiles further from the far mouth than the runner is.

FINAL_SUMMARY.headline: A tuning DOES reach parity with skills-off on the registered metric and beats it: mean per-map |WR-0.5| 0.188 (skills off) -> 0.078 (recommended dict) / 0.065 (with destiny dropped from the tagger kit). Passes 1 and 2 selected on mean win rate, which is NOT the registered metric, and both were worse than skills off (0.215 / 0.240).

journey_verdict.castability_caveat: Lv3 0.22 and Foundry 0.17 casts/round are below the 0.3 bar under the recommended tuning; the other five maps are 0.55-1.86.
journey_verdict.summary: Kit-dependent, and the pass-2 verdict ('journey pulls its weight') was true only on mean win rate. On the registered metric journey is a small LIABILITY under the full kit and an ASSET under the recommended one, because it is a variance lever: it pushed Spiral from 0.721 to 0.871 (overshoot) when destiny was live, and lifts the weak maps when it is not.

limits: Atrium is unreachable by any tuning: 0.113 off, 0.200 recommended, and it supplies the max |err| of every configuration. It needs a map change.
The recommendation effectively deletes one of the four abilities. Balance and gameplay value conflict here, and this document picks balance because that is what was registered.
Round length stays 38% short of skills-off (25.0 s vs 40.1 s); that cost is not in the registered metric.
The dial-only form relies on ChasePolicy not gating without vision. A trained tagger may gate anyway at REVEAL 0, in which case the dial form and the kit change diverge and this needs re-measuring.

objective.registered: balance_error = |runner_win_rate - 0.5|, PER MAP (docs/study-e-protocol.md §2); aggregated as the mean over the 7-map suite, with median/max/RMSE reported alongside.
objective.why_not_mean_wr: A mean of win rates lets an overshoot cancel an undershoot: Spiral 0.871 hid Warren 0.100 and the pair read as balanced. In the registered metric they add.

dead_dials.DESTINY_MIN/MAX/PREFERRED_DIST: raising MIN past 5 makes ChasePolicy gate itself away from the runner, because it compares against the imported module constant DESTINY_MAX_DIST=5. Worth +12 pp to the runner but turns destiny's one-out ablation negative.
dead_dials.JOURNEY_DEPTH: no measurable effect at 5 vs the shipped 3 — the shipped maps have no 4-5 tile wall block between two open regions.
dead_dials.STASIS_RANGE: inert at or above TILE*4.5 (ChasePolicy.STASIS_CAST caps the cast distance: 180/200/320 px give bit-identical rounds); below it the tagger asks 127 casts per round and is refused all of them, standing still ~8 s. Not a balance dial.
